prompt: Order the Scrum events as they happen within one Sprint.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.
task.explanation: The Sprint starts with Sprint Planning, Daily Scrums run throughout, the Review inspects the increment, and the Retrospective closes the Sprint.

prompt: The Scrum Guide sets maximum timeboxes for a one-month Sprint: Planning 8 h, Review 4 h, Retrospective 3 h, Daily Scrum 15 min. For shorter Sprints, events are usually shorter. Your team runs 2-week Sprints and scales Planning, Review and Retro to half the monthly maximum. What are their timeboxes?

task.prompt: Calculate each value from the data.
task.explanation: Half of 8, 4 and 3 hours is 4, 2 and 1.5 hours. The Daily Scrum stays at 15 minutes whatever the Sprint length.

prompt: Here is how an agency team describes its Scrum events. Mark the statements that do not match the Scrum Guide.

task.prompt: Mark every segment that is a problem. Leave the sound ones unmarked.

segments.text: The Sprint Review is a working session where stakeholders see the increment and discuss what to do next.
The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute status report to the PM.
segments.issue: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their plan, not a status report.

segments.text: The Retrospective plans ways to improve quality and effectiveness.
When work is not finished, we extend the Sprint by a few days.
segments.issue: Sprints have a fixed length; unfinished work returns to the Product Backlog.

segments.text: Sprint Planning produces a Sprint Goal and a Sprint Backlog.
The Sprint itself is a container for all the other events.

prompt: Your 2-week Sprint Reviews have become 15-minute demos where the client watches silently and leaves.

task.prompt: Your 2-week Sprint Reviews have become 15-minute demos where the client watches silently and leaves.

steps.question: What is missing?
options: Stakeholder collaboration on what to do next, based on what was done
A longer slide deck
More features in the demo
A bigger audience
steps.explanation: The Review is a working session to inspect the outcome and adapt the backlog, not a one-way demo.

steps.question: What change do you make for the next Review?
options: Let the client use the increment, then discuss feedback and adjust the top of the backlog together
Send a video instead and cancel the meeting
Have only the PM present
Add a status report
steps.explanation: Hands-on use and backlog discussion turn it into a real inspection and adaptation.

prompt: Mid-Sprint, the client tells the Product Owner that a new regulation makes the Sprint Goal (a new referral programme) pointless.

task.prompt: Mid-Sprint, the client tells the Product Owner that a new regulation makes the Sprint Goal (a new referral programme) pointless.

steps.question: What can happen to the Sprint?
options: The Product Owner can cancel it because the Sprint Goal is obsolete
The Scrum Master must extend it
The Developers must finish it anyway
The client cancels it directly
steps.explanation: Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint, and only if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

steps.question: What happens next?
options: Done work is reviewed, unfinished items go back to the Product Backlog, and a new Sprint Planning starts
The team takes a week off
All work is thrown away
The old Sprint Backlog is kept unchanged
steps.explanation: Cancelling returns undone work to the Product Backlog and the team plans a new Sprint.

prompt: Order the three topics of Sprint Planning as the Scrum Guide presents them.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.

items.label: What can be Done this Sprint? (select items)
Why is this Sprint valuable? (Sprint Goal)
How will the chosen work get done? (plan the work)

task.explanation: Planning starts with the why (the Sprint Goal), then selects what, then the Developers plan how.

prompt: What is the purpose of the Sprint Retrospective?

options: To plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness
To demo features to the client
To estimate the backlog
To assign blame for missed items
mcq.explanation: The Retrospective inspects how the last Sprint went regarding people, interactions, processes and tools, and identifies improvements.

prompt: Who must attend the Daily Scrum?

options: The Developers
The client sponsor
The whole agency
Only the Scrum Master
mcq.explanation: The Daily Scrum is for the Developers; the Scrum Master and Product Owner take part as Developers only if they work on Sprint Backlog items.

prompt: Your team suggests skipping the Retrospective when 'nothing went wrong'. What is the best response?

options: Keep it; there is always something to improve, and good practices are worth reinforcing
Skip it to save time
Replace it with an extra demo
Hold it only once a quarter
mcq.explanation: Retrospectives are where the team continuously improves; a good Sprint still offers improvements and practices to keep.
